newsitem.title: GERMANY: Brau und Brunnen 1996 loss widens.
newsitem.headline: Brau und Brunnen 1996 loss widens.

text.p: German drinks group Brau und Brunnen AG, majority-owned by Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel-Bank AG, said on Wednesday its group loss widened to 228.9 million marks ($134.4 million) in 1996 and that it had used up all its reserves at parent company level.
At parent company level, Brau und Brunnen made a loss of 179.5 million marks in 1996, the company said in a mandatory statement released after a meeting of its supervisory board.
In 1995, the company made a loss of 181.2 million marks at group level and 161.4 million marks at parent company level.

The company said the group loss stemmed from extraordinary costs of 306 million marks which resulted from the restructuring of its brewing division as well as from writedowns and provisions set aside for real estate holdings.

That stood against extraordinary income of 221 million marks from the sale of real estate as well as the sale of stakes in East Europe and in two German companies, Heidelberger Schlossquell-Brauerei and Schwarzwald-Sprudel.
The company also said it would ask shareholders to approve the creation of 100 million marks of authorised capital to last five years.
"This authorised capital is intended to create room for manoeuvre in the medium term. It will under no circumstances be used in the current year," the statement said.
Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel-Bank said on Tuesday it was open to discussions on the sale of its 58 percent stake in Brau und Brunnen.
The bank said it had been seeking an industrial partner for the drinks group for years but had never been able to reach agreement on price or concept for a purchase.
